title: Vienna letters to Baron Schenck (1706) and ciphered letters to Hetman Sieniawski (1707-1714), Archiwum Narodowe w Krakowie (DECODE R7468-R7500)

steps.what: DECODE metadata for R7460-R7507 by API; 130 images of R7462-R7507 with the session cookie; no key or decryption file on any record.
Neighbouring records R7460-R7467 (ASang 85/3 keys, Krakow_UNK_1/2) and R7501-R7507 (Wąsowicz-Lubomirski, key R7501) checked as keys for the group.

Kaczka, Danubius XXX (2012) prints the Brâncoveanu/Cantacuzino letters of nr 13 and nr 5 from these originals with keys A and B; nothing on the Schenck letters, R7475, R7476, R7481-R7482, R7484-R7485.
Two subagents transcribed the 15 Schenck letters (52 images) with cipher runs, codes, superscripts and dockets; letters are dated Vienna, not Dresden.
Free many-to-one homophonic annealing (de-1740s, order 5, unigram prior) on the 642 run tokens then available.
Run endings 19 43, 21 45, 20 44, 19 55 and the clustering of frequent numbers suggest homophones on consecutive numbers in alphabetical order.

Annealing only the 23 block boundaries of an alphabetical key over 1-84 (monotone.py): best restart gives blocks of three from a=7-9; 'der Baron Kleinburg alhier', 'correspondenz', 'seiner proposition'.
The recipient's superscripts over three runs of R7486 (s a k l a, p r e t, a u f) agree with the block key.

Second pass over every run against the key at full resolution: 24 lines corrected (scribe's 31 written like 21, delta-shaped 6); 79=z, 70=w, 76-78=y confirmed; 9 runs (48 numbers) still give no sense.
Kaczka's key A and the R7475 table scored on the Schenck runs with de-1740s: -5.6 and -7.0 per character against -2.8 for the block key.
Code values from context: 189 = Baron Schenck, 190 = King of Sweden, 150 = King Augustus, 100 = the Imperial court; 208 = 'der Kayser' from the recipient's gloss. The other 72 codes left open.
R7473 p. 17, ten lines decoded with Kaczka's key A agree with the interlinear gloss and his printed text.

Subagents transcribed the unprinted Sieniawski pieces with their interlinear decipherments: R7475 (alphabetical homophonic table rebuilt from the gloss), R7476 and R7484-R7485 (Chomentowski's 3-digit syllabary, syllabary.tsv), R7481-R7482 (key B).
Second context pass: two subagents re-read at full resolution every sentence with a code or a dotted sign in the 15 letters (transcr/CTX_R74xx.txt, ~90 crops); corrections written back.
The recipient's gloss in R7493 re-read: 'der' over the sign o. and 'von Kayser' over '5 83': o. = der, 5 = von, 83 = der Kayser; the earlier 208 = der Kayser withdrawn.
190 = Charles XII withdrawn (the King of Sweden is named in clear in the same letter; 190 is an imperial minister); 204 = Schweden from 'zu timide wegen 204' and 'jalousie'.

Alphabetical order of the nomenclator: the 500s rise with the alphabet (509 Friede < 513 Ordre < 515 Progressen < 519 Reise < 524 Urlaub), bounding 502 Abreise, 518 Recommendation, 521 Resolution; the 100s-200s are not one alphabetical run (204 Schweden breaks it), so no person was valued from position.
Dotted signs as a word code: o. = der (gloss), L. = und, f. = bey, b. = von dem; d., e., g., c., m., p., oo, ooo, oj, 3., 2. left open (no single value fits their contexts).

Wiener Diarium 1706 on ANNO for dated cribs: blocked by a Cloudflare Turnstile check; searches for Schenck, 'Sidon', 'Seligman', Saxon-Vienna correspondence 1706 and the Repertorium der diplomatischen Vertreter: nothing usable (Saxon envoys at Vienna: Wackerbarth to 1706, Vesnich 1706-08, not tied to any code).

R7476: faint glosses re-read at high contrast (34 crops), then a language pass using the alphabetical bands of the syllabary: 84.8% then 88.5% of 1,622 tokens read; letter re-dated to May-Aug 1714 (code XVIII glossed 'Hospodar Multański', Brâncoveanu in Yedikule).
R7481, R7482, R7484, R7485 checked token by token against gloss and key (encipherment slips settled): 99.6%, 100%, 95.9%, 100% read as sense.
R7484 pass 3: code 76 = ferman from two glosses, the f band and R7476; 'stambulscy'; LM scoring and the embassy literature (Perłakowski 2020) gave nothing for the rest: 96.5%.

R7476 passes 4-6: unread stretches re-transcribed digit by digit at 2.5-3x (closed 7 read as 4 six times, other look-alikes), glosses re-read, Polish words scored with lang/ pl-modern, names checked against Perłakowski 2020: 88.5% -> 88.9% -> 92.9% -> 94.4% (1,531 of 1,621); codes 135 Kanclerz, 215 Porta, 280 u, 310 x added.

Chomentowski embassy 1712-14 for names as cribs: Perłakowski 2020 names Jan Spiegel ('Pan Szpigieł') and Franciszek Goltz; no other name matched the unread syllables (Poniatowski, Kapudan, kajmakam, Bender, Białogród, Gdańsk, Pułtawa tried).

outcome.method_basis: The Schenck letters' 2-digit letter table (alphabetical blocks of three) was recovered here by annealing the block boundaries on a German n-gram model, with no crib; the recipient's few superscripts and glosses agree with it and give o. = der, 5 = von, 83 = der Kayser.
outcome.fraction_read_source: measure.py: Schenck letters, 1,361 cipher tokens = 682 letter-cipher numbers + 545 code numbers (3-digit and small word codes) + 134 dotted signs; read = 638 numbers in runs giving sense + 151 code tokens + 76 signs with a value

parts.label: Vienna to Baron Schenck, 1706
parts.basis: letter table recovered by monotone annealing; 93.5% of the letter-cipher numbers read in sense; 63.6% of all 1,361 tokens; 65 of 77 three-digit codes (persons) open

parts.label: Brâncoveanu and Cantacuzino to Sieniawski, 1709-1714
parts.basis: printed by Kaczka 2012 from these originals with key A; sample checked here

parts.label: unprinted Sieniawski letters (R7475, Turculeț 1709, Chomentowski 1713)
parts.basis: contemporary interlinear decipherments transcribed and checked: R7475 ~99.6%, R7481 99.6%, R7482 100%, R7484 96.5%, R7485 100%; R7476 94.4% after six passes (74 tokens of known letters form no word)

gaps.item: Schenck letters: 65 of 77 three-digit codes (394 tokens), mostly persons: 187, 181, 166, 190, 254, 258, 132, 193, 186 ...
gaps.detail: roles fixed from context (transcr/CTX_*), names not: no key with the letters, on DECODE, in print; the 100s-200s are not in alphabetical order; the Saxon cipher keys would be in Dresden (HStA), the Wiener Diarium is behind a bot check

gaps.item: Schenck letters: dotted signs d., e., g., c., m., p., oo, ooo, oj and small codes 3., 2. (about 90 tokens)
gaps.detail: articles or pronouns; no single value fits every occurrence, no gloss

gaps.item: Schenck letters: 8 letter-cipher runs (44 numbers) without sense (lceth, ditlan, gutswor ...)
gaps.detail: digits confirmed twice on the images; single short runs, probably names or slips, no second occurrence
letters known from gloss or key but no word, after digit re-transcription at 3x, band alternatives and LM scoring

gaps.item: R7476: 8 tokens in names (p. 32 L9-10, code 216)
gaps.detail: glossed syllables; no matching name in the embassy literature
one-off codes, no gloss, no band value
margin number p. 31 L32, stroke p. 32 L13, gloss over 112 at 3x
three short passages whose syllables are certain but whose words are not recovered
gloss a flourish unreadable at 3.5x; R7476's only 112 also illegibly glossed

outcome.notes: R7468-R7500 are four collections: the Schenck letters (AKM 21), Zbiór Dzieduszyckich 26/32 nr 13 and nr 5, and 24/11 no. 116 (R7484-R7485, misnamed Krakow_UNK on DECODE). Pass 2 (coordinator's request for a full reading): 62.4% -> 63.6% on the Schenck letters with the dotted signs now counted as tokens.

prior.where: Sieniawski group: Kaczka, Danubius XXX (2012) printed the Brâncoveanu/Cantacuzino letters and keys A and B; interlinear contemporary decipherments on R7475, R7476, R7481-R7485. Schenck letters: none found (no key, edition or DECODE reading).

human: Project-level: DECODE login cookie supplied and the target assigned in a brief (catalogue entry 333). No target-specific intervention.
